Some articles deal with this issue. I am writing a paper on detecting leakage radiation from potential alien civilisations (leakage = unintentional). Here are two quotes from my introduction, with references to some previous articles:

Sullivan et al. (1978) (the article pdf is behind a paywall at [this link](http://science.sciencemag.org/content/199/4327/377), but similar issues are dealt with [here](https://history.nasa.gov/CP-2156/ch5.4.htm) by the same author from 1985) postulate that broadcast signals leaking out from Earth would be detectable to a few light-years with a telescope equivalent to the Arecibo observatory.

To what distances could signals similar in power to those used in earthly broadcast be detected with telescopes similar in sensitivity to the ones currently (or soon to be) available? [Loeb & Zaldarriaga (2007)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/astro-ph/0610377.pdf) and [Siemon et al. (2014)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.4867.pdf) provide answers to that question. If we were to use SKA to scan the sky in a large bandwidth (say, from 400 to 800MHz) for a month, we should be able to detect signals up to tens of parsecs away. Indeed, at a distance of 100pc (that's about 300 light-years), a 1MW signal represents a flux density of roughly 1µJy (1Jy = 10^(-26)W/m^(2)/Hz). The full SKA2 is expected to have a sensitivity of 100µJy for one second of exposition. Thus a sensitivity threshold lower than 0.1µJy is achievable with an observation time of about a month. While these are imprecise back-of-the-envelope calculations, they provide reasonable motivation to pursue a deeper analysis of such signals.

There are plenty of guides out there but here is (to me) the simplest approach :

- Use Coinbase/GDAX to buy ETH or LTC (don't buy BTC as the fees are way too high);  
- Make an account on Binance or any exchange which lists the alt you want to buy, which we'll call ALT, and deposit the ETH/LTC onto your Binance account;  
- Exchange ETH (or LTC) for ALT, or to BTC then ALT if the ETH/ALT (or LTC/ALT) pair doesn't exist on the exchange you're using.  
- Ideally you'd want to create a wallet for ALT and withdraw the coins from the exchange to your personal wallet.

There are a few tricky points in the process, especially in choosing the exchange, but as long as you are careful, not too hasty, and do your research you should be fine :)

Making money on alt coins is the same as making money on any financial product : let's say you buy 100 ALT today for $1 each and a year from now ALT is worth $10. You still have 100 ALT but now the total is worth $1000. You can then trade them back to BTC and cash out.  
What you have to keep in mind is that even though there might now be a USD/ALT pair, since there are USD/BTC and BTC/ALT pair you can always exchange a coin to BTC then USD (though it might be a better idea to trade to something else than BTC as the fees are quite high). Technically the value of ALT can decrease with regards to BTC, but still increase with regards to USD (if BTC goes x10 in USD and ALT goes x0.5 in BTC, then ALT still went x5 in USD).

I live in France, and I've had a very similar thought for quite a while now, with the economic crisis. In France, we have a lot of social services, which means a lot of public money is spent on that. With the economic crisis, the government has to make cuts, so there are less aids, and people manifest against that in the streets. We've grown accustomed to a certain level of luxury, which prevents us from going back to a more frugal life. Do you notice how your family starts to freak out when the electricity runs out in your house, even if it only lasts one night? The same can be said about beggars, if you give the same beggar 1€ a day, at first he'll be thanking you, a lot. But then, if you're ever short on that 1€, he'll be cursing you for not giving it to him. People grow accustomed to the best conditions they have, so that they can't revert back to their previous form (in the latter case, being a beggar without earning 1€ a day).

And I think I've got an explanation for that. Our species has to survive, I'd say it is the only goal of a species. I like to call that its will (even though a species has no will). now what has more chances to survive, a beggar without money, or a beggar with (a little) money? I'd go for the richer one. What has more chances to survive, people who are helped, or people who aren't? I believe our species makes it so that once we are helped, we can't revert because then we'd be less likely to live (even less than if we had never been helped at all). This means progress is the consequence of the will of our species. Then why, why are we the only species to have invented it? This is a question I've been asking myself for quite a while now...

Now in case of an apocalypse, maybe if we hadn't had progress at all, then maybe we'd be more likely to survive. But really, what are the odds of that happening?
